1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Corner plots + tau(nu) ladder from joint-fit posterior samples.
3	
4	Reads <RUNS>/data/joint/<b>_joint_samples.npz (samples, weights, param_names,
5	alpha_bounds) written by run_joint_fit.py. Produces:
6	  <OUT>/<b>_corner.png      focused corner: tau_1ghz, alpha, the fit's zeta params
7	                            (shared zeta_1ghz/x_zeta or per-band zeta_C/D), dDM_C/D
8	  <OUT>/tau_nu_ladder.png   tau(nu)=tau_1ghz*nu^-alpha, all sightlines, 68% band
9	
10	  python plot_joint_posteriors.py [b1 b2 ...]
11	"""
12	
13	import os
14	import sys
15	
16	import matplotlib
17	import numpy as np
18	
19	matplotlib.use("Agg")
20	import corner
21	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
22	from _figsave import save_fig
23	from dynesty.utils import resample_equal
24	
25	RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
26	OUT = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
27	BURSTS = sys.argv[1:] or ["johndoeII", "wilhelm", "phineas", "oran"]
28	
29	LABELS = {
30	    "tau_1ghz": r"$\tau_{1\,\rm GHz}$ (ms)",
31	    "alpha": r"$\alpha$",
32	    "zeta_C": r"$\zeta_{\rm C}$",
33	    "zeta_D": r"$\zeta_{\rm D}$",
34	    "zeta_1ghz": r"$\zeta_{1\,\rm GHz}$",
35	    "x_zeta": r"$x_\zeta$",
36	    "delta_dm_C": r"$\delta{\rm DM}_{\rm C}$",
37	    "delta_dm_D": r"$\delta{\rm DM}_{\rm D}$",
38	}
39	
40	
41	def focus_for(names):
42	    # shared zeta(nu) fit carries zeta_1ghz/x_zeta; per-band fit carries zeta_C/D
43	    z = ["zeta_1ghz", "x_zeta"] if "zeta_1ghz" in names else ["zeta_C", "zeta_D"]
44	    return ["tau_1ghz", "alpha", *z, "delta_dm_C", "delta_dm_D"]
45	
46	
47	COLORS = {"johndoeII": "C0", "wilhelm": "C1", "phineas": "C2", "oran": "C3"}
48	
49	
50	def load(b):
51	    d = np.load(f"{OUT}/{b}_joint_samples.npz", allow_pickle=True)
52	    names = list(d["param_names"])
53	    eq = resample_equal(d["samples"], d["weights"])  # equal-weight posterior
54	    return names, eq, tuple(float(x) for x in d["alpha_bounds"])
55	
56	
57	def corner_one(b):
58	    names, eq, abnd = load(b)
59	    focus = focus_for(names)
60	    idx = [names.index(n) for n in focus]
61	    sub = eq[:, idx]
62	    K = len(focus)
63	    fig = corner.corner(
64	        sub,
65	        labels=[LABELS[n] for n in focus],
66	        show_titles=True,
67	        title_fmt=".2f",
68	        quantiles=[0.16, 0.5, 0.84],
69	        title_kwargs={"fontsize": 9},
70	        label_kwargs={"fontsize": 10},
71	    )
72	    axd = fig.axes[1 * K + 1]  # alpha diagonal panel (FOCUS idx 1)
73	    for e in abnd:
74	        axd.axvline(e, color="r", ls=":", lw=1)  # alpha prior edges
75	    a_med = float(np.median(sub[:, 1]))
76	    fig.suptitle(f"{b}: joint corner  (alpha~U{abnd}, median={a_med:.2f})", fontsize=12)
77	    fp = save_fig(fig, f"{OUT}/{b}_corner", dpi=110)
78	    plt.close(fig)
79	    print(f"  wrote {fp}  alpha_med={a_med:.2f}")
80	    return names, eq
81	
82	
83	def tau_ladder(bursts_data):
84	    nu = np.linspace(0.40, 1.55, 200)
85	    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
86	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.2))
87	    for b, (names, eq) in bursts_data.items():
88	        it, ia = names.index("tau_1ghz"), names.index("alpha")
89	        n = min(4000, eq.shape[0])
90	        sel = rng.choice(eq.shape[0], n, replace=False)
91	        tau1, al = eq[sel, it], eq[sel, ia]
92	        T = tau1[:, None] * nu[None, :] ** (-al[:, None])  # (n, nu), ms
93	        lo, med, hi = np.percentile(T, [16, 50, 84], axis=0)
94	        c = COLORS.get(b)
95	        ax.plot(nu, med, color=c, lw=2, label=f"{b}  (alpha={np.median(al):.2f})")
96	        ax.fill_between(nu, lo, hi, color=c, alpha=0.18)
97	    ax.axvspan(0.40, 0.80, color="gray", alpha=0.08)
98	    ax.axvspan(1.28, 1.53, color="gray", alpha=0.12)
99	    xt = ax.get_xaxis_transform()
100	    ax.text(0.60, 0.95, "CHIME", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="0.4", transform=xt)
101	    ax.text(1.40, 0.95, "DSA", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="0.4", transform=xt)
102	    ax.set_yscale("log")
103	    ax.set_xlabel("frequency (GHz)")
104	    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\tau(\nu)$ (ms)")
105	    ax.set_title(r"Joint-fit $\tau(\nu)=\tau_{1\,\rm GHz}\,\nu^{-\alpha}$ ladder (68% band)")
106	    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
107	    ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
108	    fp = save_fig(fig, f"{OUT}/tau_nu_ladder", dpi=120)
109	    plt.close(fig)
110	    print(f"  wrote {fp}")
111	
112	
113	def main():
114	    data = {}
115	    for b in BURSTS:
116	        f = f"{OUT}/{b}_joint_samples.npz"
117	        if not os.path.exists(f):
118	            print(f"  MISSING {f} — skip")
119	            continue
120	        names, eq = corner_one(b)
121	        data[b] = (names, eq)
122	    if data:
123	        tau_ladder(data)
124	
125	
126	if __name__ == "__main__":
127	    main()
128	
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Posterior-predictive per-band check for the joint fits.
3	
4	Rebuilds each band's FRBModel (same prep as run_joint_fit), evaluates the M3
5	model at the JOINT best-fit medians, and reports per-band reduced chi2 +
6	profile overlays. If the joint solution fits BOTH bands well (chi2~1), the
7	shared tau*nu^-alpha (and its alpha) is a real joint measurement. If one band
8	is poorly fit, the shallow alpha is a forced compromise between irreconcilable
9	bands, not a measurement.
10	
11	  python joint_ppc.py <burst>
12	"""
13	
14	import json
15	import os
16	import sys
17	
18	import numpy as np
19	
20	REPO = os.environ.get("FLITS_REPO", "/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS")
21	RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
22	sys.path.insert(0, f"{REPO}/scattering")
23	import matplotlib
24	import yaml
25	
26	matplotlib.use("Agg")
27	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
28	from _figsave import save_fig
29	from scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams
30	from scat_analysis.config_utils import load_telescope_block
31	from scat_analysis.pipeline.io import BurstDataset
32	
33	
34	def prepare(cfg_path, name, outdir):
35	    cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(cfg_path))
36	    tel = load_telescope_block(cfg["telcfg_path"], cfg["telescope"])
37	    ds = BurstDataset(
38	        cfg["path"],
39	        outdir,
40	        name=name,
41	        telescope=tel,
42	        f_factor=int(cfg["f_factor"]),
43	        t_factor=int(cfg["t_factor"]),
44	        outer_trim=float(cfg.get("outer_trim", 0.15)),
45	        onpulse_crop=os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP", "1") == "1",
46	        onpulse_pad_factor=float(os.environ.get("FLITS_ONPULSE_PAD", "0.5")),
47	    )
48	    m = ds.model
49	    m.dm_init = float(cfg.get("dm_init", 0.0))
50	    return m
51	
52	
53	def band_chi2(model, p, gain=False):
54	    mod = model(p, "M3")
55	    if gain:  # apply profiled per-channel gain: model = g_f * K_f
56	        g = model.gain_spectrum(p, "M3")
57	        mod = g[:, None] * mod
58	    noise = np.asarray(model.noise_std, dtype=float)
59	    if noise.ndim == 1:
60	        noise = noise[:, None]
61	    r = (model.data - mod) / np.where(noise > 0, noise, np.inf)
62	    valid = model.valid
63	    if valid is not None:
64	        valid = np.asarray(valid)
65	        r = r[valid] if valid.ndim == 1 else r[valid]
66	    r = r[np.isfinite(r)]
67	    chi2 = float(np.sum(r**2))
68	    npix = int(r.size)
69	    dof = max(npix - 7, 1)
70	    return chi2 / dof, mod
71	
72	
73	def main():
74	    b = sys.argv[1]
75	    out = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
76	    cC = f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml"
77	    cD = f"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml"
78	    mC = prepare(cC, f"{b}_chime", out)
79	    mD = prepare(cD, f"{b}_dsa", out)
80	
81	    d = json.load(open(f"{out}/{b}_joint_fit.json"))
82	    p = {k: v["median"] for k, v in d["percentiles"].items()}
83	    tau, al = p["tau_1ghz"], p["alpha"]
84	    shared = bool(d.get("shared_zeta", False))  # shared zeta(nu) fit is gain-marginal
85	    gain = bool(d.get("marginalize_gain", False)) or shared
86	    # shared zeta -> per-band array zeta_1ghz*nu^x_zeta; else the stored per-band scalar
87	    zC = p["zeta_1ghz"] * np.asarray(mC.freq, float) ** p["x_zeta"] if shared else p["zeta_C"]
88	    zD = p["zeta_1ghz"] * np.asarray(mD.freq, float) ** p["x_zeta"] if shared else p["zeta_D"]
89	    if gain:
90	        pC = FRBParams(
91	            c0=1.0,
92	            t0=p["t0_C"],
93	            gamma=0.0,
94	            zeta=zC,
95	            tau_1ghz=tau,
96	            alpha=al,
97	            delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"],
98	        )
99	        pD = FRBParams(
100	            c0=1.0,
101	            t0=p["t0_D"],
102	            gamma=0.0,
103	            zeta=zD,
104	            tau_1ghz=tau,
105	            alpha=al,
106	            delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"],
107	        )
108	    else:
109	        pC = FRBParams(
110	            c0=p["c0_C"],
111	            t0=p["t0_C"],
112	            gamma=p["gamma_C"],
113	            zeta=zC,
114	            tau_1ghz=tau,
115	            alpha=al,
116	            delta_dm=p["delta_dm_C"],
117	        )
118	        pD = FRBParams(
119	            c0=p["c0_D"],
120	            t0=p["t0_D"],
121	            gamma=p["gamma_D"],
122	            zeta=zD,
123	            tau_1ghz=tau,
124	            alpha=al,
125	            delta_dm=p["delta_dm_D"],
126	        )
127	
128	    chiC, modC = band_chi2(mC, pC, gain=gain)
129	    chiD, modD = band_chi2(mD, pD, gain=gain)
130	    print(
131	        f"{b}: alpha={al:.2f} tau1={tau:.3f} | CHIME chi2/dof={chiC:.2f}  DSA chi2/dof={chiD:.2f}"
132	    )
133	
134	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 4))
135	    for a, m, mod, nm, ch in [
136	        (ax[0], mC, modC, f"CHIME chi2={chiC:.2f}", chiC),
137	        (ax[1], mD, modD, f"DSA chi2={chiD:.2f}", chiD),
138	    ]:
139	        prof_d = np.nansum(m.data, axis=0)
140	        prof_m = np.nansum(mod, axis=0)
141	        a.plot(m.time, prof_d, "k", lw=0.8, label="data")
142	        a.plot(m.time, prof_m, "r", lw=1.2, label="joint model")
143	        a.set_title(f"{b} {nm}")
144	        a.set_xlabel("time (ms)")
145	        a.legend(fontsize=8)
146	    fig.suptitle(f"{b}: joint alpha={al:.2f}, tau_1GHz={tau:.3f} ms")
147	    fig.tight_layout()
148	    fp = save_fig(
149	        fig, f"{out}/{b}_joint_ppc", dpi=110, bbox_inches=None
150	    )  # keep original (untight) crop; montage assembles these
151	    print(f"  wrote {fp}")
152	    json.dump(
153	        {"burst": b, "alpha": al, "tau_1ghz": tau, "chi2_chime": chiC, "chi2_dsa": chiD},
154	        open(f"{out}/{b}_joint_ppc.json", "w"),
155	        indent=2,
156	    )
157	
158	
159	if __name__ == "__main__":
160	    main()
161

=== _figsave.py ===
"""Save a figure in publication-vector form (PDF for LaTeX + SVG) and keep a PNG.

The Faber2026 manuscript builds with pdflatex, which embeds the PDF; SVG is the
archival vector form; the PNG stays for the HTML deck / figure-review gate. Pass
a path *stem* (extension optional/ignored). ``dpi`` applies to the PNG only —
vector formats ignore it. Returns the .pdf path (the manuscript-bound artifact).
"""

VECTOR = ("pdf", "svg")


def save_fig(fig, stem, *, png=True, dpi=110, **kw):
    stem = str(stem)
    if stem.lower().endswith((".png", ".pdf", ".svg")):
        stem = stem.rsplit(".", 1)[0]
    kw.setdefault("bbox_inches", "tight")
    for ext in VECTOR:
        fig.savefig(f"{stem}.{ext}", **kw)  # vector: dpi-independent
    if png:
        fig.savefig(f"{stem}.png", dpi=dpi, **kw)
    return f"{stem}.pdf"


def _selftest():
    import tempfile
    from pathlib import Path

    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    ax.plot([0, 1], [0, 1])
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        pdf = save_fig(fig, f"{d}/x.png", dpi=80)  # pass a .png stem on purpose
        assert pdf == f"{d}/x.pdf"
        for ext in ("pdf", "svg", "png"):
            assert Path(f"{d}/x.{ext}").exists(), ext
        plt.close(fig)
        # png=False skips the raster
        save_fig(plt.subplots()[0], f"{d}/y", png=False)
        assert Path(f"{d}/y.pdf").exists() and not Path(f"{d}/y.png").exists()
    print("ok")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _selftest()
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Build a self-contained joint-scattering slide deck (docs/joint_scattering_deck.html).
3	
4	Data-driven + idempotent: scans joint_json/*_joint_fit.json for the per-sightline
5	shared (alpha, tau_1ghz) + lnZ (summary table, ALL available bursts), joint_ppc.json
6	for per-band chi2, and dsa_figs/{b}_{joint_ppc,corner,fullband_waterfall}.png for the
7	detail slides. Re-run as more fits/figures land to auto-extend toward all 12.
8	
9	Slides: title -> method -> summary table -> tau(nu) ladder -> per-sightline detail
10	(only bursts with >=1 figure) -> caveats. Self-contained (base64 images), prev/next
11	+ arrow-key nav. Output is iframe-embedded by the 'Joint Scattering' tab in
12	docs/index.html.
13	
14	  python build_joint_deck.py
15	"""

29	    "johndoeII",

44	    "wilhelm": "Good fit; resolved scint band-width implies a DIFFERENT screen than the broadening tau.",
45	    "phineas": "Steep slope, but DSA band is the poorest fit - treat cautiously.",
46	    "oran": "alpha rails to the 1.0 floor; CHIME nuisance unconstrained -> NOT a measurement, drop.",

55	def load_fit(b):
56	    f = os.path.join(JSN, f"{b}_joint_fit.json")
57	    if not os.path.exists(f):
58	        return None
59	    d = json.load(open(f))
60	    p = d["percentiles"]
61	    a, t = p["alpha"], p["tau_1ghz"]
62	    if d.get("shared_zeta"):
63	        zc = zd = p["zeta_1ghz"]["median"]  # shared zeta(nu): the 1-GHz width
64	    else:
65	        zc, zd = p["zeta_C"]["median"], p["zeta_D"]["median"]
66	    lnz = d.get("log_evidence", float("nan"))
67	    # status, worst-first: prior rails and unphysical intrinsic width are
68	    # disqualifying; a wide posterior or an anomalous evidence is a warning.
69	    if a["lower"] <= ALO + 0.05:
70	        status, scls = "rails alpha=1 floor", "bad"
71	    elif a["upper"] >= AHI - 0.05:
72	        status, scls = "rails alpha=6 ceiling", "bad"
73	    elif max(zc, zd) > 3.0:
74	        status, scls = "zeta runaway (unphysical)", "bad"
75	    elif (a["upper"] - a["lower"]) > 2.0:
76	        status, scls = "alpha unconstrained", "warn"
77	    elif lnz < -1e5:
78	        status, scls = "anomalous lnZ", "warn"
79	    else:
80	        status, scls = "clean", "ok"
81	    return dict(
82	        burst=b,
83	        a=a["median"],
84	        alo=a["lower"],
85	        ahi=a["upper"],
86	        tau=t["median"],
87	        tlo=t["lower"],
88	        thi=t["upper"],
89	        ddmC=p["delta_dm_C"]["median"],
90	        ddmD=p["delta_dm_D"]["median"],
91	        zc=zc,
92	        zd=zd,
93	        lnz=lnz,
94	        status=status,
95	        scls=scls,
96	    )
97

140	  <p class="sub">Measuring the scattering index &alpha; (&tau;&prop;&nu;<sup>&minus;&alpha;</sup>)
141	     directly from the ~1&nbsp;GHz cross-band &tau; lever</p>
142	  <p class="big">{n_fit} / 12 sightlines fit &middot; {n_clean} give a clean &alpha; ({crange}); the rest rail the prior or show unphysical widths</p>
143	  <p class="foot">shared (&tau;<sub>1GHz</sub>, &alpha;) + per-telescope (c0, t0, &gamma;, &zeta;, &delta;DM) &middot; dynesty nested sampling &middot; &alpha;~U[1,6]</p>
144	</section>""")
145	
146	# S2 method
147	slides.append("""
148	<section class="slide">
149	  <h2>Why a joint fit</h2>
150	  <ul>
151	    <li>A <b>single band</b> fixes only the product &tau;&middot;&nu;<sup>&minus;&alpha;</sup> at its own frequency &mdash; &alpha; and &tau; are degenerate.</li>
152	    <li>Fitting CHIME (~0.6&nbsp;GHz) and DSA (~1.4&nbsp;GHz) <b>together</b> with a shared (&tau;<sub>1GHz</sub>, &alpha;) breaks the degeneracy: the ratio &tau;<sub>C</sub>/&tau;<sub>D</sub> pins the slope.</li>
153	    <li>Intrinsic / timing params (c0, t0, &gamma;, &zeta;, &delta;DM) stay <b>per telescope</b> &mdash; they absorb band-specific structure; only scattering + dispersion are shared.</li>
154	    <li>Caveat: with 16 ch/band the lever is effectively <b>2-point</b> &mdash; &alpha; is driven by the cross-band &tau; ratio, so per-band fit quality matters.</li>

"""Synthesis figures for the joint CHIME-DSA scattering ladder.
Reads *_joint_fit*.json in this dir; writes PNGs to figs_ladder/.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

D = os.path.dirname(__file__)
OUT = os.path.join(D, "figs_ladder")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)


def load():
    rows = {}
    for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(D, "*_joint_fit*.json")):
        d = json.load(open(f))
        m = re.match(r"(.+?)_joint_fit_?(.*)\.json", os.path.basename(f))
        burst, tag = m.group(1), (m.group(2) or "base")
        a = d.get("alpha", {})
        rows[(burst, tag)] = dict(
            a=a.get("median"),
            ep=a.get("err_plus"),
            em=a.get("err_minus"),
            tau=(d.get("tau_1ghz") or {}).get("median"),
            lnZ=d.get("log_evidence"),
            C=d.get("components_C"),
            D=d.get("components_D"),
            s2=d.get("gain_s2"),
        )
    return rows

=== local hpcc-run CLI ===
#!/bin/bash
# hpcc-run — run a command on the held flits-dev compute node, non-interactive.
# Brain stays local (Claude Code / Codex); this is the agent's hands on HPCC.
# Pairs with hpcc-dev (which holds the node + interactive tmux dashboard).
#
# Usage:
#   hpcc-run '<command>'          run on the held flits-dev compute node
#   hpcc-run --login '<command>'  run on the login node (light builds/tests only)
#
# The Mac can't ssh the compute node directly (key won't auth there), so node
# commands nest Mac -> hpcc(login) -> node, exactly as hpcc-dev documents.
set -euo pipefail
SSH="ssh -o BatchMode=yes hpcc"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--login" ]; then
  shift
  exec $SSH "$*"
fi

[ $# -gt 0 ] || { echo "hpcc-run: no command given" >&2; exit 2; }

NODE=$($SSH "squeue -h -n flits-dev -u \$USER -t RUNNING -o '%N'" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | tr -d ' ')
[ -n "$NODE" ] || { echo "hpcc-run: no running flits-dev node — run 'hpcc-dev' first to hold one." >&2; exit 1; }

# ponytail: base64 the command so arbitrary quotes/pipes survive the double SSH
# hop unmangled — naive nested-quoting (what hpcc-dev uses for fixed commands)
# breaks the moment an agent passes a command containing quotes.
CMD_B64=$(printf '%s' "$*" | base64 | tr -d '\n')
exec $SSH "ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $NODE 'echo $CMD_B64 | base64 -d | bash'"

Kept here to avoid editing the\n    # under-review joint_ppc.py.\n    d = json.load(open(f\"{OUT}/{b}_joint_fit.json\"))\n    p = {k: v[\"median\"] for k, v in d[\"percentiles\"].items()}\n    tau, al = p[\"tau_1ghz\"], p[\"alpha\"]\n    shared = bool(d.get(\"shared_zeta\", False))\n    gain = bool(d.get(\"marginalize_gain\", False)) or shared\n    zC = p[\"zeta_1ghz\"] * np.asarray(mC.freq, float) ** p[\"x_zeta\"] if shared else p[\"zeta_C\"]\n    zD = p[\"zeta_1ghz\"] * np.asarray(mD.freq, float) ** p[\"x_zeta\"] if shared else p[\"zeta_D\"]\n\n    def band(suf, z):\n        c0 = 1.0 if gain else p[f\"c0_{suf}\"]\n        gam = 0.0 if gain else p[f\"gamma_{suf}\"]\n        return FRBParams(\n            c0=c0, t0=p[f\"t0_{suf}\"], gamma=gam, zeta=z,\n            tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=p[f\"delta_dm_{suf}\"],\n        )\n\n    return band(\"C\", zC), band(\"D\", zD), tau, al, gain\n\n\ndef main():\n    n = len(BURSTS)\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(n, 2, figsize=(11, 2.6 * n), squeeze=False)\n    for i, b in enumerate(BURSTS):\n        cC = f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml\"\n        cD = f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml\"\n        mC = prepare(cC, f\"{b}_chime\", OUT)\n        mD = prepare(cD, f\"{b}_dsa\", OUT)\n        pC, pD, tau, al, gain = joint_params(b, mC, mD)\n        chiC, modC = band_chi2(mC, pC, gain=gain)\n        chiD, modD = band_chi2(mD, pD, gain=gain)\n        print(f\"{b}: alpha={al:.2f} tau1={tau:.3f} | CHIME {chiC:.2f}  DSA {chiD:.2f}\")\n        for ax, m, mod, lab, chi in [\n            (axes[i][0], mC, modC, \"CHIME\", chiC),\n            (axes[i][1], mD, modD, \"DSA\", chiD),\n        ]:\n            ax.plot(m.time, np.nansum(m.data, axis=0), \"k\", lw=0.8, label=\"data\")\n            ax.plot(m.time, np.nansum(mod, axis=0), \"r\", lw=1.2, label=\"joint model\")\n            ax.set_title(f\"{b} {lab}  $\\\\chi^2$={chi:.2f}\", fontsize=10)\n            ax.set_xlabel(\"time (ms)\", fontsize=8)\n            if i == 0 and lab == \"CHIME\":\n                ax.legend(fontsize=7)\n    fig.suptitle(\n        r\"Joint CHIME$\\times$DSA posterior-predictive (model at joint $\\tau_{1\\rm GHz},\\alpha$ medians)\",\n        fontsize=12,\n    )\n    fig.tight_layout()\n    fp = save_fig(fig, f\"{OUT}/joint_ppc_montage\", dpi=110)\n    print(f\"  wrote {fp}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"

# VERDICT

**Canonical family for the manuscript joint figures: `sharedzeta + exp-exp PBF` (all-exponential), per-burst best-model — NOT `base`.** This is a *recorded, accepted decision*, not my call: **ADR-0003** (`docs/adr/0003-single-exponential-pbf.md:19-23`) states "Fit **every band with a single exponential thin-screen PBF**… All citable α come from the all-exp campaign; **no mixed-PBF or all-power-law α is quoted in the manuscript**." The **base** family is the mixed-PBF default (CHIME power-law / DSA exp), which ADR-0003 calls "physically incoherent" and explicitly **supersedes**.

The base-family figures currently committed in `dsa_figs/` (`joint_ppc_montage.png`, `*_joint_ppc.png`) and the Jun-24 08:38 HPCC PPCs are rendered from the **superseded** family. **Do not ship them as-is.**

But there is a hard blocker for one figure (oran/phineas), detailed in §4.

## 2. Which numbers the figures should show

The base α values currently rendered (oran 5.96 ceiling, johndoeII 1.06) are **wrong by the project's own accepted decision**. The figures should show the **all-exp** column: johndoeII 1.57, **oran 2.66 (not 5.96)**, wilhelm 2.56, phineas 3.43.

The single largest consequence: **oran un-rails from α=5.96 to α=2.66** once the 2nd CHIME component + exp PBF are used. The base-family "oran rails the ceiling" panel is an artifact of the mixed PBF + missing component, not physics.

---

## 3. Should oran/wilhelm appear in the montage?

**Keep both, but their canonical (all-exp) status differs from what the base figures imply:**

=== ADR-0003 (canonical PBF decision) ===
# Adopt a single exponential pulse-broadening function for both bands

**Status:** accepted

## Context

The default joint fitter used a **mixed PBF** — CHIME power-law, DSA exponential.
That default is physically incoherent: a single sightline samples one scattering
medium, so the PBF *functional form* is fixed by the screen geometry and only its
timescale τ scales with frequency. The per-band preference that motivated the
default (e.g. wilhelm, ΔlnZ ≈ +4 for per-band over all-exponential) is the model
using PBF-shape freedom to absorb band-specific *profile* structure — overfitting,
not medium physics. The all-exp campaign (`ALLEXP_PBF_RUN.md`, 2026-06-24) showed
the PBF choice is a *dominant* α systematic for marginal bursts while immaterial
for clean ones.

## Decision

Fit **every band with a single exponential thin-screen PBF**
(`--pbf-C exp --pbf-D exp`). All citable α come from the all-exp campaign; no
mixed-PBF or all-power-law α is quoted in the manuscript. For the well-constrained
single-screen sightlines the choice is immaterial (|Δα| ≤ 0.1); it matters only
where multiplicity or low S/N already preclude a citable α.

## Consequences

- `results/joint_fit_summary.md` and `joint_gate_verdicts.md` must be regenerated
  from all-exp fits; mixed-PBF α are superseded (tracked follow-up).
- The marquee profile-bias demonstrator **moves off zach onto whitney
  (FRB 20220310F)**: zach's multiplicity correction *reverses sign* with the PBF
  (mixed 3.32→2.41 vs all-exp 3.319→4.59), so it is unreliable as a clean
  demonstrator and is **withheld** (see [0004](0004-l1-sub-kolmogorov-alpha-floor.md)
  context and the decision map). whitney's second DSA component is confirmed real
  (ΔlnZ +2706/+2683/+2671 across s²=1/10/100, no sign-flip), so its α 1.5→5.12
  unrailing is real physics, not a prior artifact.
- The manuscript states the PBF choice explicitly (`budget.tex` PBF argument) and
  cites the |Δα| ≤ 0.1 robustness for the well-constrained set (done, Faber2026
  PR #9).
- Reproducibility hazard to fix: two s²-grid generations coexist — stale
  mixed-PBF `analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/joint_ladder/*_s2-*.json` (which
  `_s2verdict.py` reads by default) vs the canonical all-exp grids
  (`joint_ladder/allexp_json/*_pbf-exp-exp.json`, already local). The stale set
  must be deleted or `_s2verdict.py` repointed (tracked follow-up). The zach all-exp
  C2D3 grid is already pulled and adjudicated (rescue fails → single-comp α=3.319,
  `ALLEXP_PBF_RUN.md:106`).
=== ADR-0004 head ===
# L1 sub-Kolmogorov α-floor policy

**Status:** accepted (panel recommendation 2026-06-24; code/verdict implementation deferred)

## Context

The operative joint-fit L1 gate hard-FAILs α below **1.5** — hardcoded
`ALPHA_MIN, ALPHA_MAX = 1.5, 6.0` in
`analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/gate_joint_committed.py:26`, which produced the
committed `joint_gate_verdicts.md` (johndoeII 1.373, oran 1.439, whitney 1.458 all
"FAIL | L1 alpha=… outside (1.5,6.0)"). Note the floor is **not** in
`flits/fitting/VALIDATION_THRESHOLDS.py`: its `ALPHA_MARGINAL_MIN = 2.0` has **zero
Python consumers** (a dead constant), and the "1.5 < α < 6.0" bound in
`.cursor/rules/AGENT_CONFIGURATION_FLITS.md:97` is prose that happens to match the
real gate while the same contract's pseudocode (line 249) and L3 text (line 307)
say 2.0 — a pre-existing doc inconsistency. The single operative number is 1.5, in
`gate_joint_committed.py`. johndoeII reads **α ≈ 1.37** — adversarially trusted
(2026-06-19, 4-lens workflow; α=4 rejected at Δ(−2lnL) ≈ 2400) as a genuine
sub-Kolmogorov measurement, and *un-railed* under the prior `alpha_bounds = [1.0,
6.0]` with a tight ±0.05 posterior and clean cross-band χ², so it FAILs only on the
1.5 floor. That floor conflates a *physical-impossibility* bound with a
*Kolmogorov-prior* bound and has no first-principles basis: a Kolmogorov thin
screen gives α = 4.4, a square-law spectrum α = 4.0, but multi-screen, anisotropic,
or inner-scale-truncated media flatten the observed index well below 2, and
sub-Kolmogorov indices are observed in the FRB/pulsar literature. FAILing α = 1.37
rejects a measurement for being *informative* (sub-Kolmogorov is the regime the
two-band lever arm exists to probe), not for being unphysical.

## Decision

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Corner plots + tau(nu) ladder from joint-fit posterior samples.
3	
4	Reads <RUNS>/data/joint/<b>_joint_samples.npz (samples, weights, param_names,
5	alpha_bounds) written by run_joint_fit.py. Produces:
6	  <OUT>/<b>_corner.png      focused corner: tau_1ghz, alpha, the fit's zeta params
7	                            (shared zeta_1ghz/x_zeta or per-band zeta_C/D), dDM_C/D
8	  <OUT>/tau_nu_ladder.png   tau(nu)=tau_1ghz*nu^-alpha, all sightlines, 68% band
9	
10	  python plot_joint_posteriors.py [b1 b2 ...]
11	"""
12	
13	import os
14	import sys
15	
16	import matplotlib
17	import numpy as np
18	
19	matplotlib.use("Agg")
20	import corner
21	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
22	from _figsave import save_fig
23	from dynesty.utils import resample_equal
24	
25	RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
26	OUT = f"{RUNS}/data/joint"
27	BURSTS = sys.argv[1:] or ["johndoeII", "wilhelm", "phineas", "oran"]
28	
29	LABELS = {
30	    "tau_1ghz": r"$\tau_{1\,\rm GHz}$ (ms)",
31	    "alpha": r"$\alpha$",
32	    "zeta_C": r"$\zeta_{\rm C}$",
33	    "zeta_D": r"$\zeta_{\rm D}$",
34	    "zeta_1ghz": r"$\zeta_{1\,\rm GHz}$",
35	    "x_zeta": r"$x_\zeta$",
36	    "delta_dm_C": r"$\delta{\rm DM}_{\rm C}$",
37	    "delta_dm_D": r"$\delta{\rm DM}_{\rm D}$",
38	}
39	
40	
41	def focus_for(names):
42	    # shared zeta(nu) fit carries zeta_1ghz/x_zeta; per-band fit carries zeta_C/D
43	    z = ["zeta_1ghz", "x_zeta"] if "zeta_1ghz" in names else ["zeta_C", "zeta_D"]
44	    return ["tau_1ghz", "alpha", *z, "delta_dm_C", "delta_dm_D"]
45	
46	
47	COLORS = {"johndoeII": "C0", "wilhelm": "C1", "phineas": "C2", "oran": "C3"}
48	
49	
50	def load(b):
51	    d = np.load(f"{OUT}/{b}_joint_samples.npz", allow_pickle=True)
52	    names = list(d["param_names"])
53	    eq = resample_equal(d["samples"], d["weights"])  # equal-weight posterior
54	    return names, eq, tuple(float(x) for x in d["alpha_bounds"])
55	
56	
57	def corner_one(b):
58	    names, eq, abnd = load(b)
59	    focus = focus_for(names)
60	    idx = [names.index(n) for n in focus]
61	    sub = eq[:, idx]
62	    K = len(focus)
63	    fig = corner.corner(
64	        sub,
65	        labels=[LABELS[n] for n in focus],
66	        show_titles=True,
67	        title_fmt=".2f",
68	        quantiles=[0.16, 0.5, 0.84],
69	        title_kwargs={"fontsize": 9},
70	        label_kwargs={"fontsize": 10},
71	    )
72	    axd = fig.axes[1 * K + 1]  # alpha diagonal panel (FOCUS idx 1)
73	    for e in abnd:
74	        axd.axvline(e, color="r", ls=":", lw=1)  # alpha prior edges
75	    a_med = float(np.median(sub[:, 1]))
76	    fig.suptitle(f"{b}: joint corner  (alpha~U{abnd}, median={a_med:.2f})", fontsize=12)
77	    fp = save_fig(fig, f"{OUT}/{b}_corner", dpi=110)
78	    plt.close(fig)
79	    print(f"  wrote {fp}  alpha_med={a_med:.2f}")
80	    return names, eq
81	
82	
83	def tau_ladder(bursts_data):
84	    nu = np.linspace(0.40, 1.55, 200)
85	    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
86	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5.2))
87	    for b, (names, eq) in bursts_data.items():
88	        it, ia = names.index("tau_1ghz"), names.index("alpha")
89	        n = min(4000, eq.shape[0])
90	        sel = rng.choice(eq.shape[0], n, replace=False)
91	        tau1, al = eq[sel, it], eq[sel, ia]
92	        T = tau1[:, None] * nu[None, :] ** (-al[:, None])  # (n, nu), ms
93	        lo, med, hi = np.percentile(T, [16, 50, 84], axis=0)
94	        c = COLORS.get(b)
95	        ax.plot(nu, med, color=c, lw=2, label=f"{b}  (alpha={np.median(al):.2f})")
96	        ax.fill_between(nu, lo, hi, color=c, alpha=0.18)
97	    ax.axvspan(0.40, 0.80, color="gray", alpha=0.08)
98	    ax.axvspan(1.28, 1.53, color="gray", alpha=0.12)
99	    xt = ax.get_xaxis_transform()
100	    ax.text(0.60, 0.95, "CHIME", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="0.4", transform=xt)
101	    ax.text(1.40, 0.95, "DSA", ha="center", fontsize=9, color="0.4", transform=xt)
102	    ax.set_yscale("log")
103	    ax.set_xlabel("frequency (GHz)")
104	    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\tau(\nu)$ (ms)")
105	    ax.set_title(r"Joint-fit $\tau(\nu)=\tau_{1\,\rm GHz}\,\nu^{-\alpha}$ ladder (68% band)")
106	    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
107	    ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")
108	    fp = save_fig(fig, f"{OUT}/tau_nu_ladder", dpi=120)
109	    plt.close(fig)
110	    print(f"  wrote {fp}")
111	
112	
113	def main():
114	    data = {}
115	    for b in BURSTS:
116	        f = f"{OUT}/{b}_joint_samples.npz"
117	        if not os.path.exists(f):
118	            print(f"  MISSING {f} — skip")
119	            continue
120	        names, eq = corner_one(b)
121	        data[b] = (names, eq)
122	    if data:
123	        tau_ladder(data)
124	
125	
126	if __name__ == "__main__":
127	    main()
128	
```

1	# All-exponential PBF ladder rerun — HPCC campaign (2026-06-24)
2	
3	PBF = pulse-broadening function; lnZ = log Bayesian evidence.
4	
5	## Purpose
6	
7	Every joint CHIME–DSA fit in the original ladder used the `run_joint_fit.py`
8	default of a **mixed** PBF — `--pbf-C powerlaw --pbf-D exp` (CHIME a Kolmogorov
9	power-law tail, DSA an exponential). That default is physically incoherent: a
10	single burst on a single sightline sees one scattering medium, so the PBF
11	*functional form* is fixed by the screen geometry and only its timescale τ scales
12	with frequency. A power-law tail at CHIME and an exponential at DSA cannot both
13	describe the same screen. The per-band preference that motivated the default
14	(wilhelm, ΔlnZ ≈ +4.0 for per-band over all-exponential) is the model using PBF
15	shape freedom to absorb band-specific *profile* structure — overfitting, not
16	medium physics.
17	
18	This run re-fits the whole ladder under the **physical all-exponential PBF**
19	(`--pbf-C exp --pbf-D exp`), changing only the PBF and holding each burst's
20	best-model configuration, α-prior, and gain treatment fixed, so that
21	α_exp − α_mixed isolates the PBF systematic per burst.
22	
23	## Design and provenance
24	
25	- **Driver:** dynamic workflow `allexp-ladder` (run `wf_4b71052d-9b7`; 17 agents,
26	  ~33 min wall) — Submit → Drain (poll `squeue`) → per-burst Verify → Synthesize.
27	- **Compute:** Caltech HPCC, `partition=expansion`, via
28	  `/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/run_joint.sbatch` (8 cores, 16 GB,
29	  30 min default).
30	- **Per-burst command** (model flags from each burst's ladder best-model;
31	  α-bounds [1.5, 6.0] throughout):
32	
33	  ```
34	  sbatch run_joint.sbatch <burst> 600 <model-flags> \
35	         --alpha-lo 1.5 --alpha-hi 6.0 --pbf-C exp --pbf-D exp
36	  ```
37	
38	  sharedzeta bursts (`--shared-zeta`): freya, casey, chromatica, wilhelm,
39	  hamilton. Component bursts (`--marginalize-gain --components-C X
40	  --components-D Y`): mahi (C1D1 `--force-multi`), phineas (C3D3), oran (C2D1),
41	  isha (C2D1), zach (C2D3), johndoeII (C2D1). whitney was done separately on the
42	  local machine (C2D2, re-prepped) and is folded in for completeness.
43	- **Output naming:** the PBF-tracking edit (this session) records
44	  `pbf_C/pbf_D/beta_C/beta_D` in each JSON and auto-suffixes non-default PBF runs,
45	  so all outputs land as `<burst>_joint_fit_<tag>_pbf-exp-exp.json` with no
46	  clobber of the mixed-default files. Verdicts computed by
47	  `/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs/_allexp_verify.py` and independently
48	  re-checked from the JSONs (10/10 α match).
49	
50	## Results
51	
52	α_mixed is the original mixed-PBF ladder value; α_exp is this run. "railed/wide"
53	flags a posterior whose median sits within 3σ of a prior bound (1.5 or 6.0) —
54	either a hard pin or a wide tail that reaches the bound.
55

59	| isha | 5.39 | 5.48 +0.42/−1.98 | +0.09 | wide → upper | done |
60	| freya | 4.36 | 4.356 ± 0.04 | −0.004 | no | done |
61	| phineas | 3.33 | 3.426 ± 0.05 | +0.096 | no | done (job 64538743) — PBF-robust |

72	different normalizations, so lnZ is comparable only exp-vs-mixed *within* a burst,
73	not across the column.)
74	
75	## Interpretation
76	
77	1. **The PBF systematic is small for the well-constrained bursts.** The six
78	   un-railed bursts — freya, casey, chromatica, wilhelm, oran, and whitney — move
79	   by |Δα| ≤ 0.09 between the mixed and physical PBF. Their published α are
80	   *confirmed, not overturned*; the all-exp values agree and become canonical for
81	   physical consistency.
82	2. **The per-band PBF was immaterial to the science.** wilhelm — the burst whose
83	   +4.0 evidence justified the mixed default — has α 2.56 → 2.558 under all-exp.
84	   The per-band PBF should be dropped: it neither changes a result nor reflects a
85	   physical screen.
86	3. **mahi is a new concern.** Under all-exp its α falls 3.80 → 3.17 and the
87	   posterior widens to +1.47/−1.18, reaching the prior floor. mahi's α is
88	   PBF-sensitive and poorly constrained once the unphysical CHIME power-law tail
89	   is removed; it needs a re-prep / model re-check (as whitney did), not a simple
90	   value swap.
91	4. **isha, johndoeII, hamilton are unconstrained under either PBF.** isha rails
92	   the upper bound with a wide lower tail; johndoeII and hamilton are hard-pinned
93	   at the 1.5 floor. No PBF choice rescues them.
94

136	## Manuscript joint figures — regeneration runbook

139	`tau_nu_ladder.png`, `joint_ppc_montage.png`, and the per-burst `*_joint_ppc.png`.

162	  (`FLITS_ONPULSE_CROP` default `"1"` in `run_joint_fit.py:47` and `joint_ppc.py:45`;

180	## Verdict
181	
182	The physical all-exp PBF **confirms seven well-constrained bursts** (freya, casey,
183	chromatica, wilhelm, oran, whitney, phineas; |Δα| ≤ 0.1) — these are publishable.
184	**Five block the ladder:** **zach** (Δα +2.18, the marquee profile-bias number was
185	PBF-confounded — single-comp all-exp α = 3.319 ≈ single-comp mixed 3.32, so the
186	multiplicity correction *reverses* sign with the PBF and the "biases high" thesis
187	does not survive; needs the all-exp fixed-s2 component-count check before any
188	claim), **mahi** (Δα −0.63,
189	wide/floor), **isha** (wide/upper), and **johndoeII**, **hamilton** (hard-railed at

1	#!/usr/bin/env python
2	"""Multi-component joint-fit model vs data overlay (gain-marginal).
3	
4	Reconstructs the fitted N-component model per band from the saved MEDIAN params
5	using the SAME kernel construction (model(.,"M3")) and the SAME ridge gain solve
6	as the canonical _gain_marginal_multi_band, at that routine's profiled s2.
7	NOTE: the per-channel per-component gains absorb the burst spectrum + scint, so
8	the freq-collapsed profile matches data by construction -- the figure shows
9	component placement and the shared scattering tail, not an absolute misfit test.
10	
11	  python model_overlay.py <burst> <tag>     # tag like C2D3, C4D1
12	"""
13	
14	import json
15	import os
16	import re
17	import sys
18	from dataclasses import replace
19	
20	import matplotlib
21	import numpy as np
22	
23	matplotlib.use("Agg")
24	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
25	
26	REPO = os.environ.get("FLITS_REPO", "/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS")
27	RUNS = os.environ.get("FLITS_RUNS", "/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs")
28	sys.path.insert(0, RUNS)
29	sys.path.insert(0, f"{REPO}/scattering")
30	from run_joint_fit import prepare  # identical band prep as the fit
31	from scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams
32	from scat_analysis.burstfit_joint import _gain_marginal_multi_band
33	
34	burst, tag = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
35	mt = re.match(r"C(\d+)D(\d+)", tag)
36	nC, nD = int(mt.group(1)), int(mt.group(2))
37	J = json.load(open(f"{RUNS}/data/joint/{burst}_joint_fit_{tag}.json"))
38	P = {k: v["median"] for k, v in J["percentiles"].items()}
39	tau, alpha = P["tau_1ghz"], P["alpha"]
40	
41	
42	def band_params(prefix, n, ddm):
43	    return [
44	        FRBParams(
45	            c0=1.0,
46	            t0=P[f"t0_{prefix}{i}"],
47	            gamma=0.0,
48	            zeta=P[f"zeta_{prefix}{i}"],
49	            tau_1ghz=tau,
50	            alpha=alpha,
51	            delta_dm=ddm,
52	        )
53	        for i in range(1, n + 1)
54	    ]
55	
56	
57	def solve_band(model, ps):
58	    valid = model.valid
59	    Ks = np.stack([model(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), "M3", freq_subset=valid) for p in ps])
60	    d = model.data[valid]
61	    sig = np.clip(model.noise_std[valid], 1e-9, None)
62	    var = sig**2
63	    b = np.einsum("nft,ft->fn", Ks, d)
64	    M = np.einsum("nft,mft->fnm", Ks, Ks)
65	    _, diag = _gain_marginal_multi_band(model, ps, ["M3"] * len(ps), s2=None)  # profiled s2
66	    s2 = diag["s2"]
67	    N = Ks.shape[0]
68	    A = M + (var / s2)[:, None, None] * np.eye(N)[None]
69	    g = np.linalg.solve(A, b[:, :, None])[:, :, 0]  # (F, N) MAP gains
70	    pred = np.einsum("fn,nft->ft", g, Ks)
71	    comps = g.T[:, :, None] * Ks  # (N, F, T)
72	    resid = d - pred
73	    chi2 = float(np.sum((resid / sig[:, None]) ** 2) / resid.size)
74	    return dict(d=d, pred=pred, comps=comps, t=model.time, sig=sig, chi2=chi2, N=N, s2=s2)

{
  "file_path": "/Users/jakobfaber/Developer/repos/github.com/jakobtfaber/dsa110-FLITS/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06/joint_ladder/_tau_ladder_allexp.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Canonical all-exp tau(nu) ladder (ADR-0003).\n\ntau(nu) = tau_1ghz * nu^-alpha for the seven well-constrained bursts whose\nall-exp single-exp-PBF fits the ALLEXP_PBF_RUN.md verdict marks publishable\n(|Delta-alpha_exp-mixed| <= 0.1). tau_1ghz/alpha are shared scalars, present in\nevery joint posterior regardless of component count, so the ladder needs no\nmodel rebuild -- just the canonical all-exp .npz per burst.\n\nHeterogeneous per-burst model: sharedzeta (freya/casey/chromatica/wilhelm) or\ncomponent (oran C2D1, phineas C3D3). whitney (C2D2, fit locally) is absent from\nHPCC -> rendered when its local .npz is located.\n\n  python _tau_ladder_allexp.py [b1 b2 ...]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport matplotlib\nimport numpy as np\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nfrom dynesty.utils import resample_equal\n\nsys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))  # _figsave\nfrom _figsave import save_fig\n\nRUNS = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_RUNS\", \"/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs\")\nOUT = f\"{RUNS}/data/joint\"\n\n# canonical all-exp posterior .npz per burst (ALLEXP_PBF_RUN.md per-burst model)\nNPZ = {\n    \"freya\": \"freya_joint_samples_sharedzeta_pbf-exp-exp.npz\",\n    \"casey\": \"casey_joint_samples_sharedzeta_pbf-exp-exp.npz\",\n    \"chromatica\": \"chromatica_joint_samples_sharedzeta_pbf-exp-exp.npz\",\n    \"wilhelm\": \"wilhelm_joint_samples_sharedzeta_pbf-exp-exp.npz\",\n    \"oran\": \"oran_joint_samples_C2D1_pbf-exp-exp.npz\",\n    \"phineas\": \"phineas_joint_samples_C3D3_pbf-exp-exp.npz\",\n    # whitney: C2D2 all-exp fit locally; .npz not on HPCC -> add when located\n}\nBURSTS = sys.argv[1:] or list(NPZ)\nCOLORS = dict(zip(NPZ, plt.cm.turbo(np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, len(NPZ)))))\n\n\ndef load(b):\n    d = np.load(f\"{OUT}/{NPZ[b]}\", allow_pickle=True)\n    names = list(d[\"param_names\"])\n    eq = resample_equal(d[\"samples\"], d[\"weights\"])  # equal-weight posterior\n    return names.index(\"tau_1ghz\"), names.index(\"alpha\"), eq\n\n\ndef main():\n    nu = np.linspace(0.40, 1.55, 200)\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.0, 5.4))\n    for b in BURSTS:\n        f = f\"{OUT}/{NPZ[b]}\"\n        if not os.path.exists(f):\n            print(f\"  MISSING {f} -- skip\")\n            continue\n        it, ia, eq = load(b)\n        n = min(4000, eq.shape[0])\n        sel = rng.choice(eq.shape[0], n, replace=False)\n        tau1, al = eq[sel, it], eq[sel, ia]\n        T = tau1[:, None] * nu[None, :] ** (-al[:, None])  # (n, nu), ms\n        lo, med, hi = np.percentile(T, [16, 50, 84], axis=0)\n        c = COLORS[b]\n        ax.plot(nu, med, color=c, lw=2, label=f\"{b}  ($\\\\alpha$={np.median(al):.2f})\")\n        ax.fill_between(nu, lo, hi, color=c, alpha=0.15)\n    ax.axvspan(0.40, 0.80, color=\"gray\", alpha=0.08)\n    ax.axvspan(1.28, 1.53, color=\"gray\", alpha=0.12)\n    xt = ax.get_xaxis_transform()\n    ax.text(0.60, 0.96, \"CHIME\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=9, color=\"0.4\", transform=xt)\n    ax.text(1.40, 0.96, \"DSA\", ha=\"center\", fontsize=9, color=\"0.4\", transform=xt)\n    ax.set_yscale(\"log\")\n    ax.set_xlabel(\"frequency (GHz)\")\n    ax.set_ylabel(r\"$\\tau(\\nu)$ (ms)\")\n    ax.set_title(r\"All-exp joint-fit $\\tau(\\nu)=\\tau_{1\\,\\rm GHz}\\,\\nu^{-\\alpha}$ ladder (68% band)\")\n    ax.legend(fontsize=8, ncol=2)\n    ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which=\"both\")\n    fig.tight_layout()\n    fp = save_fig(fig, f\"{OUT}/tau_nu_ladder_allexp\", dpi=120)\n    print(f\"  wrote {fp}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python\n\"\"\"Canonical all-exp joint-PPC montage (ADR-0003).\n\nOne row per burst: [CHIME | DSA] freq-collapsed profile, data vs reconstructed\njoint model at the posterior medians, with per-band reduced chi2 on the fit's\non-pulse-crop window (crop ON -- run_joint_fit/joint_ppc default; reproduces the\ndocumented chi2). Heterogeneous all-exp inputs, dispatched on fit type:\n\n  sharedzeta -> single component, zeta(nu)=zeta_1ghz*nu^x_zeta, gain via\n                gain_spectrum  (joint_ppc.band_chi2, gain=True)\n  component  -> N-component scalar zeta_C{i}/zeta_D{j}, gain-marginal ridge solve\n                at profiled s2  (model_overlay.solve_band, inlined below)\n\n  python _ppc_montage_allexp.py [b1 b2 ...]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom dataclasses import replace\n\nimport matplotlib\nimport numpy as np\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\nREPO = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_REPO\", \"/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS\")\nRUNS = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_RUNS\", \"/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs\")\nsys.path.insert(0, f\"{REPO}/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06\")  # _figsave, joint_ppc\nsys.path.insert(0, f\"{REPO}/scattering\")\nfrom _figsave import save_fig\nfrom joint_ppc import band_chi2, prepare  # fit-consistent prep + sharedzeta chi2\nfrom scat_analysis.burstfit import FRBParams\nfrom scat_analysis.burstfit_joint import _gain_marginal_multi_band\n\nOUT = f\"{RUNS}/data/joint\"\n\n# canonical all-exp model per burst (ALLEXP_PBF_RUN.md); whitney (C2D2, local) absent on HPCC\nSPEC = {\n    \"freya\": (\"sharedzeta\", \"sharedzeta\"),\n    \"casey\": (\"sharedzeta\", \"sharedzeta\"),\n    \"chromatica\": (\"sharedzeta\", \"sharedzeta\"),\n    \"wilhelm\": (\"sharedzeta\", \"sharedzeta\"),\n    \"oran\": (\"component\", \"C2D1\"),\n    \"phineas\": (\"component\", \"C3D3\"),\n}\nBURSTS = sys.argv[1:] or list(SPEC)\n\n\ndef jpath(b, tag):\n    return f\"{OUT}/{b}_joint_fit_{tag}_pbf-exp-exp.json\"\n\n\ndef medians(b, tag):\n    d = json.load(open(jpath(b, tag)))\n    return d, {k: v[\"median\"] for k, v in d[\"percentiles\"].items()}\n\n\ndef solve_band(model, ps):\n    # ponytail: copied verbatim from model_overlay.solve_band -- that module runs\n    # `burst, tag = sys.argv[1:]` at import, so it cannot be imported. Same gain-\n    # marginal ridge solve at profiled s2 as the canonical multi-component fit.\n    valid = model.valid\n    Ks = np.stack([model(replace(p, c0=1.0, gamma=0.0), \"M3\", freq_subset=valid) for p in ps])\n    d = model.data[valid]\n    sig = np.clip(model.noise_std[valid], 1e-9, None)\n    var = sig**2\n    b = np.einsum(\"nft,ft->fn\", Ks, d)\n    M = np.einsum(\"nft,mft->fnm\", Ks, Ks)\n    _, diag = _gain_marginal_multi_band(model, ps, [\"M3\"] * len(ps), s2=None)  # profiled s2\n    s2 = diag[\"s2\"]\n    N = Ks.shape[0]\n    A = M + (var / s2)[:, None, None] * np.eye(N)[None]\n    g = np.linalg.solve(A, b[:, :, None])[:, :, 0]  # (F, N) MAP gains\n    pred = np.einsum(\"fn,nft->ft\", g, Ks)\n    resid = d - pred\n    chi2 = float(np.sum((resid / sig[:, None]) ** 2) / resid.size)\n    return model.time, np.nansum(d, 0), np.nansum(pred, 0), chi2\n\n\ndef shared_profiles(b, P, mC, mD):\n    tau, al = P[\"tau_1ghz\"], P[\"alpha\"]\n\n    def band(suf, m):\n        z = P[\"zeta_1ghz\"] * np.asarray(m.freq, float) ** P[\"x_zeta\"]\n        p = FRBParams(\n            c0=1.0, t0=P[f\"t0_{suf}\"], gamma=0.0, zeta=z,\n            tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=P[f\"delta_dm_{suf}\"],\n        )\n        chi, mod = band_chi2(m, p, gain=True)\n        return m.time, np.nansum(m.data, 0), np.nansum(mod, 0), chi\n\n    return band(\"C\", mC), band(\"D\", mD)\n\n\ndef comp_profiles(b, P, tag, mC, mD):\n    nC, nD = int(tag[1]), int(tag[3])\n    tau, al = P[\"tau_1ghz\"], P[\"alpha\"]\n\n    def ps(prefix, n, ddm):\n        return [\n            FRBParams(\n                c0=1.0, t0=P[f\"t0_{prefix}{i}\"], gamma=0.0, zeta=P[f\"zeta_{prefix}{i}\"],\n                tau_1ghz=tau, alpha=al, delta_dm=ddm,\n            )\n            for i in range(1, n + 1)\n        ]\n\n    return (\n        solve_band(mC, ps(\"C\", nC, P.get(\"delta_dm_C\", 0.0))),\n        solve_band(mD, ps(\"D\", nD, P.get(\"delta_dm_D\", 0.0))),\n    )\n\n\ndef main():\n    n = len(BURSTS)\n    fig, axes = plt.subplots(n, 2, figsize=(11, 2.5 * n), squeeze=False)\n    for i, b in enumerate(BURSTS):\n        kind, tag = SPEC[b]\n        mC = prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml\", f\"{b}_chime\", OUT)\n        mD = prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml\", f\"{b}_dsa\", OUT)\n        d, P = medians(b, tag)\n        al, tau = P[\"alpha\"], P[\"tau_1ghz\"]\n        if kind == \"sharedzeta\":\n            (tC, dC, mCp, chiC), (tD, dD, mDp, chiD) = shared_profiles(b, P, mC, mD)\n        else:\n            (tC, dC, mCp, chiC), (tD, dD, mDp, chiD) = comp_profiles(b, P, tag, mC, mD)\n        print(f\"{b} ({kind} {tag}): alpha={al:.2f} tau1={tau:.3f} | CHIME {chiC:.2f}  DSA {chiD:.2f}\")\n        for ax, t, dp, mp, lab, chi in [\n            (axes[i][0], tC, dC, mCp, \"CHIME\", chiC),\n            (axes[i][1], tD, dD, mDp, \"DSA\", chiD),\n        ]:\n            ax.plot(t, dp, \"k\", lw=0.8, label=\"data\")\n            ax.plot(t, mp, \"r\", lw=1.2, label=\"joint model\")\n            ax.set_title(f\"{b} {lab} ({tag})  $\\\\chi^2$={chi:.2f}\", fontsize=9)\n            ax.set_xlabel(\"time (ms)\", fontsize=8)\n            ax.margins(x=0)\n            if i == 0 and lab == \"CHIME\":\n                ax.legend(fontsize=7)\n    fig.suptitle(\n        r\"All-exp joint CHIME$\\times$DSA posterior-predictive \"\n        r\"(model at $\\tau_{1\\rm GHz},\\alpha$ medians; $\\chi^2$ on fit crop window)\",\n        fontsize=12,\n    )\n    fig.tight_layout()\n    fp = save_fig(fig, f\"{OUT}/joint_ppc_montage_allexp\", dpi=110)\n    print(f\"  wrote {fp}\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

Now your question — **yes, and it's arguably the strongest independent cross-check available.** Here's the honest assessment.

## The idea
Split each band into sub-bands, collapse each to a 1D profile, fit a 1D scattering model (intrinsic ⊗ exponential PBF) to each independently → recover τᵢ at sub-band center νᵢ → fit log τ vs log ν → α **emerges from the data** instead of being imposed by the joint model. Stitching CHIME + DSA sub-band τᵢ onto one τ(ν) preserves the full ~3.75× lever arm while making every point a model-independent measurement.

## What it genuinely validates
- **The well-constrained bursts** (freya, casey, chromatica, oran, phineas, whitney): if their per-sub-band τᵢ trace the same power law the joint fit reports, the joint α is corroborated by a method that never assumed it. This is a real, citable independent validation — exactly what the joint fits currently lack (my verify-gate "oracle" was just α-matches-runbook, which shares the npz; this would be *independent*).
- **wilhelm's DSA misfit (χ²=4.55):** sub-banding DSA tells you *why* — a τ(ν) that bends away from the power law (real) vs frequency-independent residual structure (substructure the single component misses). That's the single most useful thing it'd buy you right now.
- It cleanly separates scattering (strong ν⁻⁴-ish dependence) from achromatic intrinsic substructure — the core "profile bias" concern.

## Where it bites (real limitations, not hedging)
1. **S/N falls as √N per sub-band.** Validates the bright/well-constrained set; will *not* rescue the railed ones (johndoeII/hamilton/isha/mahi) — they're under-constrained already and get worse split.
2. **Short DSA lever + unresolved τ.** Within DSA (1.2–1.5, ν ratio 1.25 → τ ratio ~2.4×) the per-band slope is weak; worse, at 1.5 GHz τ ~ τ₁GHz/5 ≈ 0.01–0.15 ms, which for several bursts is **at or below the DSA time resolution** → those high-ν sub-bands give **upper limits, not detections**. The τ(ν) plot will have real points in CHIME and a mix of detections/limits in DSA.
3. **Multi-component bursts still need multi-component 1D fits.** oran/phineas/whitney/wilhelm: a naive single-component sub-band fit inherits the *same* profile-bias that the joint fit was built to avoid. So the 1D fit isn't automatically cleaner — it must model the sub-pulses too.
4. The 1D collapse drops the per-channel gain/scint weighting the joint fit's ridge solve uses — fine for narrow sub-bands, a small bias for wide ones.

## Infra already exists, partially
`within_chime_test.py` / `chime_subband_compare` (the section I folded into `budget.tex` this session) does the **model-free** version — tracks on-pulse *width* vs frequency, no fitted τ. The stronger version you're describing is: run the existing `burstfit` M2 (intrinsic + τ tail) on each sub-band as a narrow-freq dataset, collect τᵢ(νᵢ), overlay vs the joint power law. Reuses the whole pipeline, no new physics.

---

Want me to build it? Concretely: per-sub-band M2 fits (4× CHIME, 2–3× DSA) for the 7 publishable bursts, producing a τ(ν) overlay of the independent sub-band points against each burst's joint `τ₁GHz·ν⁻ᵅ` curve — detections vs upper limits flagged. That'd turn the joint α from "fit asserts it" into "independent sub-band τ(ν) corroborates it," and would adjudicate wilhelm directly. It's a real fit campaign (HPCC), so I'd scope it as a workflow gated on the same well-constrained set.

Acronyms: EMG — Exponentially-Modified Gaussian (Gaussian ⊗ one-sided exponential = the scattered-pulse profile); PBF — Pulse-Broadening Function; S/N — signal-to-noise.

Building it. Plan: per sub-band, collapse to 1D and fit an EMG (`scipy.stats.exponnorm` — the analytic scattered-pulse profile, τ=K·σ) with **τ free** → independent τ(νᵢ); multi-component bursts get a shared-τ sum-of-EMG with positions/widths fixed from the joint fit (robust in low S/N). Then per-burst τ(ν) overlay vs the joint `τ₁GHz·ν⁻ᵅ`, with a sub-band power-law α compared to α_joint. Fast scipy (not MCMC) → direct sweep on HPCC, not a workflow.

Single-component (sharedzeta) bursts fit mu/sigma/tau free.\n\nDetection vs upper limit: tau is a detection if tau > 2*sigma_tau and tau > 0.5*dt\n(dt = sub-band time sample); otherwise a 2-sigma upper limit (tau is unresolved at\nthat frequency -- expected at high DSA frequencies where tau ~ tau_1ghz/5).\n\n  python _subband_tau_validation.py [b1 b2 ...]\n\"\"\"\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport sys\n\nimport matplotlib\nimport numpy as np\n\nmatplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\nfrom scipy.optimize import curve_fit\nfrom scipy.stats import exponnorm\n\nREPO = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_REPO\", \"/home/jfaber/flits/dsa110-FLITS\")\nRUNS = os.environ.get(\"FLITS_RUNS\", \"/central/scratch/jfaber/flits-runs\")\nsys.path.insert(0, f\"{REPO}/analysis/scattering-refit-2026-06\")  # _figsave, joint_ppc\nsys.path.insert(0, f\"{REPO}/scattering\")\nfrom _figsave import save_fig\nfrom joint_ppc import prepare  # same band prep (BurstDataset) as the fit\n\nOUT = f\"{RUNS}/data/joint\"\n\n# burst -> (fit tag, n CHIME comps, n DSA comps); n=0 => sharedzeta single-comp free fit\nSPEC = {\n    \"freya\": (\"sharedzeta\", 0, 0),\n    \"casey\": (\"sharedzeta\", 0, 0),\n    \"chromatica\": (\"sharedzeta\", 0, 0),\n    \"wilhelm\": (\"sharedzeta\", 0, 0),\n    \"oran\": (\"C2D1\", 2, 1),\n    \"phineas\": (\"C3D3\", 3, 3),\n    \"whitney_fine\": (\"C2D2\", 2, 2),\n}\nNSUB = {\"chime\": 4, \"dsa\": 3}  # sub-bands per band (S/N-limited; DSA lever is short)\nBURSTS = sys.argv[1:] or list(SPEC)\n\n\ndef emg(t, A, mu, sigma, tau, b):\n    \"\"\"Single scattered pulse: A * EMG(mu,sigma,tau) + baseline.  tau = K*sigma.\"\"\"\n    K = max(tau, 1e-6) / max(sigma, 1e-6)\n    return A * exponnorm.pdf(t, K, loc=mu, scale=max(sigma, 1e-6)) + b\n\n\ndef emg_multi(t, mus, sigmas, amps, tau, b):\n    \"\"\"Sum of EMGs with shared tau; positions/widths fixed (multi-component).\"\"\"\n    out = np.full_like(t, b, dtype=float)\n    for mu, sig, A in zip(mus, sigmas, amps):\n        K = max(tau, 1e-6) / max(sig, 1e-6)\n        out = out + A * exponnorm.pdf(t, K, loc=mu, scale=max(sig, 1e-6))\n    return out\n\n\ndef subband_profiles(model, nsub):\n    \"\"\"Yield (nu_center_GHz, t_ms, profile, dt) for nsub equal frequency slices.\"\"\"\n    freq = np.asarray(model.freq, float)  # GHz, ascending\n    t = np.asarray(model.time, float)  # ms\n    dt = float(np.median(np.diff(t)))\n    edges = np.linspace(freq.min(), freq.max(), nsub + 1)\n    for k in range(nsub):\n        lo, hi = edges[k], edges[k + 1]\n        sel = (freq >= lo) & (freq < hi if k < nsub - 1 else freq <= hi)\n        if sel.sum() < 2:\n            continue\n        prof = np.nansum(model.data[sel], axis=0)\n        yield 0.5 * (lo + hi), t, prof, dt\n\n\ndef fit_single(t, prof, dt, mu0, sig0, tau0):\n    \"\"\"Free EMG fit; return (tau, sigma_tau).\"\"\"\n    A0 = float(np.nanmax(prof) - np.nanmedian(prof))\n    p0 = [max(A0, 1e-3), mu0, max(sig0, dt), max(tau0, dt), float(np.nanmedian(prof))]\n    lo = [0, t.min(), 0.3 * dt, 1e-4, -abs(A0)]\n    hi = [10 * abs(A0) + 1e-3, t.max(), (t.max() - t.min()), (t.max() - t.min()), abs(A0)]\n    try:\n        popt, pcov = curve_fit(emg, t, prof, p0=p0, bounds=(lo, hi), maxfev=20000)\n        return float(popt[3]), float(np.sqrt(max(pcov[3, 3], 0)))\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"      single-fit fail: {e}\")\n        return np.nan, np.nan\n\n\ndef fit_multi(t, prof, dt, mus, sigmas, tau0):\n    \"\"\"Shared-tau sum-of-EMG; positions/widths fixed. Fit amps + tau. Return (tau, sigma_tau).\"\"\"\n    n = len(mus)\n    A0 = max(float(np.nanmax(prof) - np.nanmedian(prof)), 1e-3)\n\n    def f(t_, *p):\n        amps, tau, b = p[:n], p[n], p[n + 1]\n        return emg_multi(t_, mus, sigmas, amps, tau, b)\n\n    p0 = [A0] * n + [max(tau0, dt), float(np.nanmedian(prof))]\n    lo = [0] * n + [1e-4, -abs(A0)]\n    hi = [10 * A0] * n + [(t.max() - t.min()), abs(A0)]\n    try:\n        popt, pcov = curve_fit(f, t, prof, p0=p0, bounds=(lo, hi), maxfev=30000)\n        return float(popt[n]), float(np.sqrt(max(pcov[n, n], 0)))\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"      multi-fit fail: {e}\")\n        return np.nan, np.nan\n\n\ndef joint_curve(b, tag):\n    d = json.load(open(f\"{OUT}/{b}_joint_fit_{tag}_pbf-exp-exp.json\"))\n    P = {k: v[\"median\"] for k, v in d[\"percentiles\"].items()}\n    return d, P\n\n\ndef measure_band(model, nsub, band, tag, P, ncomp):\n    \"\"\"Return arrays nu, tau, tau_err, is_det for one band's sub-bands.\"\"\"\n    nu_c, tau_v, tau_e, det = [], [], [], []\n    suf = \"C\" if band == \"chime\" else \"D\"\n    for nu, t, prof, dt in subband_profiles(model, nsub):\n        tau0 = P[\"tau_1ghz\"] * nu ** (-P[\"alpha\"])  # joint expectation (init only)\n        if ncomp == 0:  # sharedzeta single component free fit\n            mu0 = P.get(f\"t0_{suf}\", float(t[np.nanargmax(prof)]))\n            sig0 = P.get(\"zeta_1ghz\", dt * 3) * nu ** P.get(\"x_zeta\", 0.0)\n            tau, te = fit_single(t, prof, dt, mu0, max(sig0, dt), tau0)\n        else:  # multi-component: fix positions/widths from joint, fit shared tau\n            mus = [P[f\"t0_{suf}{i}\"] for i in range(1, ncomp + 1)]\n            sigmas = [max(P[f\"zeta_{suf}{i}\"], dt) for i in range(1, ncomp + 1)]\n            tau, te = fit_multi(t, prof, dt, mus, sigmas, tau0)\n        if not np.isfinite(tau) or not np.isfinite(te):\n            continue\n        is_det = (tau > 2 * te) and (tau > 0.5 * dt) and (te < tau)\n        nu_c.append(nu)\n        tau_v.append(tau)\n        tau_e.append(te)\n        det.append(bool(is_det))\n        flag = \"det\" if is_det else \"lim\"\n        print(f\"    {band} nu={nu:.3f} GHz: tau={tau:.4f}+-{te:.4f} ms [{flag}] (joint~{tau0:.4f})\")\n    return np.array(nu_c), np.array(tau_v), np.array(tau_e), np.array(det, bool)\n\n\ndef powerlaw_alpha(nu, tau, te, det):\n    \"\"\"Weighted slope of log tau vs log nu over detections -> alpha_sb, sigma_alpha.\"\"\"\n    if det.sum() < 2:\n        return np.nan, np.nan\n    x = np.log(nu[det])\n    y = np.log(tau[det])\n    w = (tau[det] / np.clip(te[det], 1e-9, None)) ** 2  # weight ~ (S/N)^2 in log\n    # weighted linear fit y = m x + c ; alpha = -m\n    W = np.sum(w)\n    mx = np.sum(w * x) / W\n    my = np.sum(w * y) / W\n    sxx = np.sum(w * (x - mx) ** 2)\n    sxy = np.sum(w * (x - mx) * (y - my))\n    m = sxy / sxx\n    # slope uncertainty from weighted residuals\n    yhat = m * (x - mx) + my\n    dof = max(det.sum() - 2, 1)\n    s2 = np.sum(w * (y[: len(x)] - yhat) ** 2) / (W * dof) if dof > 0 else np.nan\n    sm = np.sqrt(s2 / sxx) if np.isfinite(s2) else np.nan\n    return -m, sm\n\n\ndef main():\n    summary = []\n    for b in BURSTS:\n        tag, nC, nD = SPEC[b]\n        print(f\"== {b} ({tag}) ==\")\n        try:\n            mC = prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_chime_run.yaml\", f\"{b}_chime\", OUT)\n            mD = prepare(f\"{RUNS}/configs/{b}_dsa_run.yaml\", f\"{b}_dsa\", OUT)\n            d, P = joint_curve(b, tag)\n        except Exception as e:\n            print(f\"  prep/load fail: {e}\")\n            continue\n        nuC, tC, teC, dC = measure_band(mC, NSUB[\"chime\"], \"chime\", tag, P, nC)\n        nuD, tD, teD, dD = measure_band(mD, NSUB[\"dsa\"], \"dsa\", tag, P, nD)\n        nu = np.concatenate([nuC, nuD])\n        tau = np.concatenate([tC, tD])\n        te = np.concatenate([teC, teD])\n        det = np.concatenate([dC, dD])\n        a_sb, a_se = powerlaw_alpha(nu, tau, te, det)\n        a_j = P[\"alpha\"]\n        agree = (\n            \"n/a\"\n            if not np.isfinite(a_sb) or not np.isfinite(a_se) or a_se == 0\n            else f\"{abs(a_sb - a_j) / a_se:.1f} sigma\"\n        )\n        summary.append((b, a_j, a_sb, a_se, int(det.sum()), int((~det).sum()), agree))\n        # ---- per-burst tau(nu) overlay ----\n        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 5.0))\n        nug = np.linspace(0.40, 1.55, 200)\n        ax.plot(nug, P[\"tau_1ghz\"] * nug ** (-a_j), \"k-\", lw=1.6, label=f\"joint $\\\\alpha$={a_j:.2f}\")\n        for nn, tt, ee, dd, c, lab in [\n            (nuC, tC, teC, dC, \"C0\", \"CHIME sub-band\"),\n            (nuD, tD, teD, dD, \"C3\", \"DSA sub-band\"),\n        ]:\n            if len(nn) == 0:\n                continue\n            m = dd\n            if m.any():\n                ax.errorbar(nn[m], tt[m], yerr=ee[m], fmt=\"o\", color=c, ms=6, capsize=3, label=lab)\n            if (~m).any():\n                ul = np.clip(tt[~m], 0, None) + 2 * ee[~m]\n                ax.errorbar(\n                    nn[~m], ul, yerr=0.25 * ul, uplims=True, fmt=\"v\", color=c, ms=6, alpha=0.6,\n                    label=f\"{lab} (2$\\\\sigma$ u.l.)\",\n                )\n        if np.isfinite(a_sb):\n            ax.plot(nug, np.exp(np.interp(0, [0], [0])) * 0 + np.nan)  # noop keep axis\n            ttl = f\"{b}: joint $\\\\alpha$={a_j:.2f}  vs  sub-band $\\\\alpha$={a_sb:.2f}$\\\\pm${a_se:.2f}  ({agree})\"\n        else:\n            ttl = f\"{b}: joint $\\\\alpha$={a_j:.2f}  (sub-band $\\\\alpha$ unconstrained)\"\n        ax.set_yscale(\"log\")\n        ax.set_xlabel(\"frequency (GHz)\")\n        ax.set_ylabel(r\"$\\tau$ (ms)\")\n        ax.set_title(ttl, fontsize=10)\n        ax.axvspan(0.40, 0.80, color=\"gray\", alpha=0.07)\n        ax.axvspan(1.28, 1.53, color=\"gray\", alpha=0.10)\n        ax.legend(fontsize=8)\n        ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which=\"both\")\n        fig.tight_layout()\n        fp = save_fig(fig, f\"{OUT}/{b}_subband_tau\", dpi=120)\n        plt.close(fig)\n        print(f\"  wrote {fp}  joint_a={a_j:.2f} subband_a={a_sb:.2f}+-{a_se:.2f} {agree}\")\n    print(\"\\n=== SUMMARY: joint alpha vs independent sub-band alpha ===\")\n    print(f\"{'burst':12} {'a_joint':>8} {'a_subband':>16} {'ndet':>5} {'nlim':>5}  agreement\")\n    for b, aj, asb, ase, nd, nl, ag in summary:\n        sbs = f\"{asb:.2f}+-{ase:.2f}\" if np.isfinite(asb) else \"unconstrained\"\n        print(f\"{b:12} {aj:8.2f} {sbs:>16} {nd:5d} {nl:5d}  {ag}\")\n    json.dump(\n        [\n            {\"burst\": b, \"alpha_joint\": aj, \"alpha_subband\": (None if not np.isfinite(asb) else asb),\n             \"alpha_subband_err\": (None if not np.isfinite(ase) else ase), \"n_det\": nd, \"n_lim\": nl}\n            for b, aj, asb, ase, nd, nl, _ in summary\n        ],\n        open(f\"{OUT}/subband_tau_validation.json\", \"w\"),\n        indent=2,\n    )\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

> AGENT

Honest read of the run: it works, but **my validator has two bugs I must fix before trusting it** — this is exactly why the validation must itself be validated.

1. **σ_α collapses to ~0** when the power law is clean (it used residual scatter, not the τ-measurement errors) → every comparison reads as "490σ" even when α values *agree*. The sharedzeta bursts actually corroborate well: freya 3.97 vs joint 4.36, casey 2.44 vs 2.40, chromatica 3.23 vs 3.29, wilhelm 2.45 vs 2.56. Fix: weighted-LS slope error `sqrt(1/Sxx)`.
2. **Amplitude bound used peak height, not area** → for broad large-τ scattered pulses (oran CHIME τ~5 ms, whitney) the area coefficient ≫ peak, so τ pinned to 0 / blew up. (Also `A0<0` on empty sub-bands → `lo>hi` crash.) Fix: bound amplitude by integrated fluence.

166	def powerlaw_alpha(nu, tau, te, det):
167	    """Weighted slope of log tau vs log nu over detections -> alpha_sb, sigma_alpha."""
168	    if det.sum() < 2:
169	        return np.nan, np.nan
170	    x = np.log(nu[det])
171	    y = np.log(tau[det])
172	    w = (tau[det] / np.clip(te[det], 1e-9, None)) ** 2  # weight ~ (S/N)^2 in log
173	    # weighted linear fit y = m x + c ; alpha = -m
174	    W = np.sum(w)
175	    mx = np.sum(w * x) / W
176	    my = np.sum(w * y) / W
177	    sxx = np.sum(w * (x - mx) ** 2)
178	    sxy = np.sum(w * (x - mx) * (y - my))
179	    m = sxy / sxx
180	    # slope uncertainty from weighted residuals
181	    yhat = m * (x - mx) + my
182	    dof = max(det.sum() - 2, 1)

> AGENT

Now the results are sane: **casey (2.35 vs 2.40), chromatica (3.23 vs 3.29), wilhelm (2.45 vs 2.56) corroborate the joint α within ~1.5σ.** But two real issues remain:
1. **oran/whitney CHIME pin τ→0** — they're heavily scattered + faint at CHIME (joint τ~6 ms there); the fit can't find the broad tail. The danger: that produces a *spuriously tight* "upper limit" (~0.46 ms) that would **falsely appear to refute** the joint 6 ms. A failed fit must not masquerade as a refutation.
2. freya (Δα=0.38) and phineas (Δα=0.42) show mild tension — plausibly the single-EMG σ–τ degeneracy / multi-component DSA.

Adding an R² fit-quality gate so bad fits report **unconstrained** (dropped), not false limits:

Bounding by peak pinned tau->0 for oran/whitney.\n    p0 = [flu, mu0, min(max(sig0, dt), 0.5 * win), min(max(tau0, dt), 0.9 * win), base0]\n    lo = [0, t.min(), 0.3 * dt, 1e-4, base0 - flu]\n    hi = [100 * flu, t.max(), win, win, base0 + flu]\n    try:\n        popt, pcov = curve_fit(emg, t, prof, p0=p0, bounds=(lo, hi), maxfev=20000)\n        return float(popt[3]), float(np.sqrt(max(pcov[3, 3], 0)))\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"      single-fit fail: {e}\")\n        return np.nan, np.nan\n\n\ndef fit_multi(t, prof, dt, mus, sigmas, tau0):\n    \"\"\"Shared-tau sum-of-EMG; positions/widths fixed. Fit amps + tau. Bounding by peak pinned tau->0 for oran/whitney.\n    p0 = [flu, mu0, min(max(sig0, dt), 0.5 * win), min(max(tau0, dt), 0.9 * win), base0]\n    lo = [0, t.min(), 0.3 * dt, 1e-4, base0 - flu]\n    hi = [100 * flu, t.max(), win, win, base0 + flu]\n    try:\n        popt, pcov = curve_fit(emg, t, prof, p0=p0, bounds=(lo, hi), maxfev=20000)\n        return float(popt[3]), float(np.sqrt(max(pcov[3, 3], 0))), _r2(prof, emg(t, *popt))\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"      single-fit fail: {e}\")\n        return np.nan, np.nan, 0.0\n\n\ndef fit_multi(t, prof, dt, mus, sigmas, tau0):\n    \"\"\"Shared-tau sum-of-EMG; positions/widths fixed.   "old_string": "def measure_band(model, nsub, band, tag, P, ncomp):\n    \"\"\"Return arrays nu, tau, tau_err, is_det for one band's sub-bands.\"\"\"\n    nu_c, tau_v, tau_e, det = [], [], [], []\n    suf = \"C\" if band == \"chime\" else \"D\"\n    for nu, t, prof, dt in subband_profiles(model, nsub):\n        tau0 = P[\"tau_1ghz\"] * nu ** (-P[\"alpha\"])  # joint expectation (init only)\n        if ncomp == 0:  # sharedzeta single component free fit\n            mu0 = P.get(f\"t0_{suf}\", float(t[np.nanargmax(prof)]))\n            sig0 = P.get(\"zeta_1ghz\", dt * 3) * nu ** P.get(\"x_zeta\", 0.0)\n            tau, te = fit_single(t, prof, dt, mu0, max(sig0, dt), tau0)\n        else:  # multi-component: fix positions/widths from joint, fit shared tau\n            mus = [P[f\"t0_{suf}{i}\"] for i in range(1, ncomp + 1)]\n            sigmas = [max(P[f\"zeta_{suf}{i}\"], dt) for i in range(1, ncomp + 1)]\n            tau, te = fit_multi(t, prof, dt, mus, sigmas, tau0)\n        if not np.isfinite(tau) or not np.isfinite(te):\n            continue\n        is_det = (tau > 2 * te) and (tau > 0.5 * dt) and (te < tau)\n        nu_c.append(nu)\n        tau_v.append(tau)\n        tau_e.append(te)\n        det.append(bool(is_det))\n        flag = \"det\" if is_det else \"lim\"\n        print(f\"    {band} nu={nu:.3f} GHz: tau={tau:.4f}+-{te:.4f} ms [{flag}] (joint~{tau0:.4f})\")\n    return np.array(nu_c), np.array(tau_v), np.array(tau_e), np.array(det, bool)",
  "new_string": "R2_MIN = 0.5  # below this the EMG does not describe the profile -> tau unreliable, drop\n\n\ndef measure_band(model, nsub, band, tag, P, ncomp):\n    \"\"\"Return arrays nu, tau, tau_err, is_det for one band's sub-bands (bad fits dropped).\"\"\"\n    nu_c, tau_v, tau_e, det = [], [], [], []\n    n_bad = 0\n    suf = \"C\" if band == \"chime\" else \"D\"\n    for nu, t, prof, dt in subband_profiles(model, nsub):\n        tau0 = P[\"tau_1ghz\"] * nu ** (-P[\"alpha\"])  # joint expectation (init only)\n        if ncomp == 0:  # sharedzeta single component free fit\n            mu0 = P.get(f\"t0_{suf}\", float(t[np.nanargmax(prof)]))\n            sig0 = P.get(\"zeta_1ghz\", dt * 3) * nu ** P.get(\"x_zeta\", 0.0)\n            tau, te, r2 = fit_single(t, prof, dt, mu0, max(sig0, dt), tau0)\n        else:  # multi-component: fix positions/widths from joint, fit shared tau\n            mus = [P[f\"t0_{suf}{i}\"] for i in range(1, ncomp + 1)]\n            sigmas = [max(P[f\"zeta_{suf}{i}\"], dt) for i in range(1, ncomp + 1)]\n            tau, te, r2 = fit_multi(t, prof, dt, mus, sigmas, tau0)\n        if not np.isfinite(tau) or not np.isfinite(te):\n            continue\n        if r2 < R2_MIN:  # poor fit -> tau unreliable (e.g. faint/heavily-scattered CHIME); NOT a limit\n            n_bad += 1\n            print(f\"    {band} nu={nu:.3f} GHz: UNCONSTRAINED (R2={r2:.2f}<{R2_MIN}, fit fails) (joint~{tau0:.4f})\")\n            continue\n        is_det = (tau > 2 * te) and (tau > 0.5 * dt) and (te < tau)\n        nu_c.append(nu)\n        tau_v.append(tau)\n        tau_e.append(te)\n        det.append(bool(is_det))\n        flag = \"det\" if is_det else \"lim\"\n        print(f\"    {band} nu={nu:.3f} GHz: tau={tau:.4f}+-{te:.4f} ms R2={r2:.2f} [{flag}] (joint~{tau0:.4f})\")\n    return np.array(nu_c), np.array(tau_v), np.array(tau_e), np.array(det, bool), n_bad"
}

Committed `fe44b49`. (Another process committed `8886e6c` between my two commits — the branch is being actively written to; mine landed clean on top.)

## Built and run — the answer is yes, with documented limits

**Independent sub-band τ(ν) validation** of the joint α, 7 publishable bursts. The EMG fits share no machinery with the 2D joint fitter, and τ floats free per sub-band, so agreement is a real cross-check.

**3 bursts independently confirm the joint α** (within ~1.5σ): casey 2.35 vs 2.40, chromatica 3.23 vs 3.29, wilhelm 2.45 vs 2.56. The sub-band τᵢ sit on the joint power law (casey figure is textbook).

**This resolves the wilhelm flag:** its joint DSA χ²=4.55 was the worry, but its sub-band τ(ν) tracks the joint α within 1.6σ — so the DSA misfit is **profile substructure, not a scattering-vs-frequency problem**. The α is sound; the DSA residual is an unmodeled sub-pulse.

**2 mild tensions** (Δα≈0.4): freya (4.36→3.98) and phineas (3.43→3.85). Visually the CHIME points lie on the curve; the DSA points sit slightly off the steep extrapolation — consistent with the single-EMG σ–τ degeneracy (freya) and low multi-component DSA τ (phineas). Not refutations.

**2 cannot be validated by this method** — oran and whitney. At CHIME their τ~6 ms is smeared below detectability in a faint band (R²~0.1, correctly flagged *unconstrained*); at DSA τ is unresolved. Their joint α rests on the cross-band lever, which sub-banding can't reconstruct. Crucially **not refuted** — the oran DSA points lie on the joint curve; you just can't get α from the short DSA lever alone.

So: the method **independently corroborates the well-constrained core of the publishable set** and is honest about where it can't reach — exactly the marginal bursts I flagged upfront.

**Process notes** (per honest reporting): my first validator had two bugs — a σ_α that collapsed to ~0 (made agreements read as "490σ") and a peak-based amplitude bound that pinned τ→0 for broad pulses. Both fixed; I added an R²-gate so a *failed* fit reports "unconstrained" instead of a spuriously-tight limit that would falsely refute the joint fit. Caught only because I checked the validator against the runbook + visually.

**Artifacts:** `_subband_tau_validation.py` (committed), 7× `*_subband_tau.{pdf,svg,png}` + `subband_tau_validation.json` on HPCC.

This is a genuine manuscript-grade independent validation for the well-constrained bursts. Worth a short methods paragraph; I left the runbook/ledger untouched (concurrent-edit churn) — say the word and I'll fold the result in once the lane settles.

155	time $t_0$, intrinsic width $\zeta$, and a residual dispersion
156	$\delta\mathrm{DM}$). The $\sim$1\,GHz lever arm between the bands measures
157	$\alpha$ directly: the ratio of the two scattering times pins the slope, while
158	the shared normalization $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ pins its value at 1\,GHz. With
159	$\alpha$ held at the Kolmogorov value $4.4$ \citep{Rickett1990}, the two bands
160	instead return $\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}}$ estimates that disagree by up to an
161	order of magnitude for the same sightline---evidence that $\alpha\neq4.4$ along
162	these lines of sight.
163	
164	The shape of the scattering tail---the pulse-broadening function (PBF)---is set
165	by the geometry of the scattering medium: a single thin screen produces an
166	exponential tail, while an extended or shallow-spectrum medium produces a heavier
167	power-law tail (Figure~\ref{fig:pbf_shapes}; \citealp[\S11.2]{Cordes2025}). Fit
168	band by band, individual bursts can appear to prefer different PBFs in the two
169	bands---for FRB~20221203A a Kolmogorov power-law improves the CHIME evidence while
170	DSA-110 rejects any tail heavier than exponential (Figure~\ref{fig:pbf_evidence}),
171	and a per-band PBF formally beats a single exponential by $\Delta\ln Z\approx+4$.
172	A single sightline, however, samples one scattering screen, whose PBF \emph{shape}
173	is fixed by its geometry; only the timescale $\tau$ scales with frequency. A PBF
174	that switches functional form between $0.6$ and $1.4$\,GHz is therefore
175	unphysical, and the per-band preference is better read as the fit absorbing
176	band-specific profile structure---an unmodeled sub-component or intrinsic
177	asymmetry---into the tail shape. We accordingly adopt a single exponential PBF for
178	both bands. Re-fitting the full sample under this physical choice moves the
179	well-constrained scattering indices by $\le0.1$ relative to the per-band fits---so
180	the simplification costs nothing for the clean sightlines---while a marginal,
181	poorly-constrained sightline shifts by ${\approx}0.6$ in $\alpha$
182	(Figure~\ref{fig:alpha_pbf}), confirming that the PBF must be fixed on physical
183	grounds before a per-sightline index is quoted.
184

187	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{pbf_shapes}

189	  intrinsic pulse convolved with a thin-screen exponential PBF (green) versus
190	  power-law-spectrum PBFs with density index $\beta=3.00$ and $\beta=11/3$
191	  (Kolmogorov). Smaller $\beta$ yields a heavier $t^{-\beta/2}$ tail; $\beta\to4$
192	  recovers the exponential \citep[\S11.2]{Cordes2025}.}
193	  \label{fig:pbf_shapes}
194	\end{figure}
195	
196	\begin{figure*}
197	  \centering
198	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\textwidth]{wilhelm_pbf_evidence}

200	  log-evidence relative to the exponential PBF versus power-law index $\beta$ (best
201	  single-component, per band). CHIME (400--800\,MHz) mildly prefers a Kolmogorov
202	  tail ($\Delta\ln Z=+6.2$ at $\beta=11/3$); DSA (1.2--1.5\,GHz) rejects
203	  heavier-than-exponential tails monotonically. \emph{Right:} joint CHIME+DSA
204	  evidence (C1D1). A \emph{per-band} PBF (CHIME power-law, DSA exponential) beats the
205	  all-exponential model by $\Delta\ln Z=+4.0$ ($\sim6\sigma$), whereas a global
206	  power-law loses $84$. Taken at face value this favors a per-band PBF; we argue
207	  in the text that it is an unphysical artifact and adopt a single exponential PBF.}
208	  \label{fig:pbf_evidence}
209	\end{figure*}

218	  are insensitive to the choice ($|\Delta\alpha|\le0.1$); only a marginal,
219	  poorly-constrained sightline (orange) moves appreciably (${\approx}0.6$), and
220	  two sightlines are pinned at the $\alpha=1.5$ prior floor under either PBF
221	  (grey). The dashed line marks the Kolmogorov value $\alpha=4.4$.}
222	  \label{fig:alpha_pbf}
223	\end{figure}

225	A complementary, model-free check that the recovered index is not corrupted by
226	unmodelled multiplicity is to resolve each burst's profile \emph{within} the CHIME
227	band. Splitting the band into four $80\,\mathrm{MHz}$ sub-bands and tracking the
228	on-pulse width with frequency separates genuine scattering, whose width grows as
229	$\nu^{-\alpha}$, from frequency-independent intrinsic sub-structure, which does not
230	(Figure~\ref{fig:chime_subband_compare}); a burst whose sub-band widths fail to
231	scale is a candidate for hidden sub-components and is flagged before a single-screen
232	index is quoted.
233	
234	\begin{figure}
235	  \centering
236	  \includegraphics[width=0.95\columnwidth]{chime_subband_compare}
237	  \caption{Within-CHIME sub-band profiles for the co-detected FRBs johndoeII and
238	  wilhelm, each split into four $80\,\mathrm{MHz}$ sub-bands across
239	  $0.40$--$0.80\,\mathrm{GHz}$. Each panel shows the baseline-subtracted on-pulse
240	  profile against time, annotated with the model-free rms width $w_{\mathrm{rms}}$
241	  and the trailing-edge $e$-folding time $w_{\mathrm{tail}}$. A purely scattering
242	  origin predicts both widths increasing toward lower frequency as $\nu^{-\alpha}$,
243	  whereas frequency-independent intrinsic sub-structure does not; the empty
244	  $0.40$--$0.48\,\mathrm{GHz}$ sub-band for wilhelm is a data gap, not a
245	  non-detection. This profile-shape evolution is the diagnostic used to flag
246	  unmodelled temporal sub-components before a scattering index is quoted. Generated
247	  by the \texttt{dsa110-FLITS} pipeline.}
248	  \label{fig:chime_subband_compare}
249	\end{figure}
