```
251	\subsubsection{Gain-marginalized likelihood}
252	\label{sec:gainmarg}
253	
254	The per-channel amplitude of an FRB spectrum is unknown and strongly modulated
255	by scintillation; carried as a free spectral envelope it leaves correlated
256	structure in the fit residuals and invalidates a $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test.
257	We therefore marginalize the per-channel gain analytically. With a Gaussian
258	prior on the gain the per-channel evidence is available in closed form (a
259	matched-filter likelihood), and the recovered gain absorbs both the burst
260	spectrum and the scintillation pattern. This removes the spectral and
261	scintillation structure from the residual, so that the reduced $\chi^2$ and the
262	lag-1 residual autocorrelation become meaningful quality gates, and it lowers
263	the sampled dimensionality. We
264	sample the posterior by nested sampling \citep{Skilling2004}, as implemented in
265	\texttt{dynesty} \citep{Speagle2020}, and quality-gate each fit on its reduced
266	$\chi^2$ and residual whiteness, treating $R^2$ and residual normality as
267	informational.
268	
269	\subsubsection{Multiple temporal components}
270	\label{sec:multicomp}
271	
272	Some bursts comprise more than one temporal sub-component, a common feature of
273	the resolved FRB population \citep{Hessels2019, Pleunis2021}. An unmodeled
274	second component is partially absorbed by a single scattered pulse---as a steeper slope
275	and a larger scattering time---and so biases the inferred $\alpha$. We extend
276	the likelihood to $N$ temporal components per band, each contributing its own
277	$(t_0,\zeta)$ while $(\tau_{1\,\mathrm{GHz}},\alpha)$ remain shared across both
278	bands and all components, and we select the number of components per band by
279	Bayesian evidence. Because the evidence normalization differs between likelihood
280	variants, the component counts are compared on a single matched grid in which
281	even the one-component model is evaluated through the multi-component
282	likelihood, so that evidence differences are meaningful. Component arrival times
283	within a band are ordered and separated by a data-derived minimum spacing,
284	keeping the fit identifiable at every prior sample. A clean single-component
```

We split each band into sub-bands (four across CHIME, three\nacross DSA-110), collapse each to a one-dimensional profile, and fit a scattered\npulse---a Gaussian intrinsic shape convolved with a one-sided exponential tail,\nthe exponentially-modified Gaussian---to each sub-band independently, leaving the\nscattering time $\\tau$ free at every frequency. Because each $\\tau_i$ is measured\nper sub-band with no power law imposed, the slope of $\\tau_i(\\nu_i)$ is an estimate\nof $\\alpha$ that shares neither parametrization nor likelihood with the joint\ntwo-dimensional fit, so its agreement with the joint value is an independent\nvalidation rather than a self-consistency check\n(Figure~\\ref{fig:subband_tau}). For the well-constrained single-screen\nsightlines the sub-band $\\tau(\\nu)$ trace the joint power law and recover the joint\nindex to within $1.6\\sigma$ (e.g.\\ FRB~20240229A, $\\alpha=2.40$ versus\n$2.35\\pm0.03$; FRB~20221203A, $2.56$ versus $2.45\\pm0.07$). The method\nhas a built-in horizon: where a burst is faint and heavily scattered the per-sub-band\nfit cannot resolve the broad CHIME tail, and at the top of the DSA band $\\tau$ falls\nbelow the time resolution, so the most strongly scattered sightlines (e.g.\\\nFRB~20220506D) retain only DSA detections over too short a lever to constrain\n$\\alpha$ on their own---there the joint fit's cross-band lever does work that no\nsingle band can. We therefore use the sub-band reconstruction as a corroborating\ncross-check on the well-constrained indices, not as a primary estimator.\n\n\\begin{figure*}\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=0.98\\textwidth]{subband_tau_validation_grid}\n  \\caption{Independent sub-band validation of the joint scattering index. Downward triangles are $2\\sigma$ upper limits; sub-bands where the\n  scattered-pulse model does not describe the profile are dropped rather than shown\n  as limits.
